Most of the refugees were from my territory, but they also came from other territories too. Quite simply, as a person I wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What prompted you to carry out interviews in which you asked the kinds of questions that you did as to the reasons for their leaving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, precisely because I wanted -- actually, I was thinking about reasons from my point of view as commander, but I wanted to hear from these people directly, from the individuals who were leaving, what the reasons for their departure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you brought some video footage here, people leaving Kosovo to Albania. That is from the Vrbnica border post, and the date is the 13th of April, 1999. Can we see this video? It's called The Border Post of Vrbnica, the 13th of April, 1999. I'm saying this for the sake of the technical people involved, and it is actually tab 475.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Albania. This is our border post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 476 are Albanians from Prizren and released Albanians from Prizren, the 14th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You should tell us about the provenance of that video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is video footage of Radio-TV Serbia, the studio in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, it was Vrbnica.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the border post of Vrbnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that is 14 kilometres away from Prizren.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this studio from Prizren actually filmed this.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next one. That's tab 476.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So for a while they were under KLA control until the army came and drove away the KLA. That's what they're saying here.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is to the west of Prizren, Ljubizda Has, that is to say under Mount Pastrik. That's it. This is the locality. And I know that there was a terrorist group there consisting of a couple of dozen of terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain why they kept those citizens there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were groups that were getting ready from the in-depth territory to try to break into Albania, and this population from the village of Ljubizda was in the woods and they kept them as a kind of security, so as a kind of hostages, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. You brought some video footage from the road between Prizren and Djakovica on the 14th of April, the NATO bombing of civilians.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at this. That is tab 477.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could we have the provenance of the previous exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let the witness tell us about the provenance of the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And do we know the name, as a the matter of interest, of the presenters or interviewers on either of these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Like the previous one, Radio-Television Serbia, studio Prizren, Borivoje Ugrinovic is the name of the editor who filmed this footage. Sanjevic is the name of the cameraman who actually did the recording.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I hope that is sufficient information from the general.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They still work for Radio-Television Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now watch the next video clip.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the hospital in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There was no translation in a portion of this videotape. Did you hear what was said about that, how many projectiles fell?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This footage -- I said, actually, that the column was bombed in several places, stretching from Djakovica to Prizren, and this particular location was closest to Prizren, which means it was between Pirane and Landovica, by the tile factory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... video when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here on the images when it was filmed. The 14th was when the bombing took place. It was filmed on the 14th, and you were able to see the individual that I said was the editor. I mentioned him. He was there holding the microphone, and I can recognise his voice. It was Borivoje Ugrinovic. So it was Radio-Television Serbia, studio Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you brought some footage with you from the place that was bombed by NATO. It is Podrimska Street in Prizren, and the bombing took place on the 30th of April. Let's take a look at this video. It's tab 478, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During this bombing, four persons were killed and a number of people injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's the street.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are there any military facilities nearby?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a Roma settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this your medical corps, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Three languages are being spoken here; Serbian, Albanian, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and the Roma language, Romany. So they are all working together to dig up and uncover people; the police, the army, the fire brigade, all of them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mention is made here -- they're talking about digging out somebody here. Were you in Prizren on that day, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the soldiers from my medical corps could be seen, medical company, and the regular policemen, the firefighters who also belong to the police, the Roma, the Albanians, and you could hear them talking in three languages, so they were all working together to deal with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the part of the footage where you can see the whole street, can you see the whole area that was bombed, in fact, or it was a broader region that was bombed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 50 houses were destroyed in that particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just in that one strike?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just in that one strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, may we take a look at the next video segment, also of Prizren and Korisa on the 14th of May. It is tab 479. The 14th of May, 1999, is the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are people who were burnt to death.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hospital in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer is this? How much longer is this, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 30 seconds perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, were you at that place, in that location?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the next day. This happened early in the morning. People are mentioning different times here, but I think at 1230 hours on the 14th of May. It was the worst night of bombing of Prizren and the surrounding parts. The bombing went on throughout the night, and my barracks was bombed that night 47 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the barracks was empty?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was empty. Only the equipment and various installations within the barracks were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. All this footage that we have just seen, what does it represent in its totality?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They show NATO strikes on civilian targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were there casualties on the 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These people here say that casualties number over 100. However, the losses although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... position.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between 80 and 85. Because some people were completely incinerated so that the exact number could not be established. And over 100 were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we will now move to our next subject. The document I would like to look at is in tab 480. Could you tell us what kind of order is this to the military police company to initiate proceedings between Pristina military court. It was issued by you on the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order specifically pertaining to the military police company, which was duty-bound to ensure that members of the army act lawfully, because the military police also has personnel dealing with combatting crime, performing on-site investigations, and other jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say: "The examples of a great number of members of the VJ as a whole and of a great number of members of our unit ... are shining ones. Despite such results achieved and the high moral values which are a credit to the members of our unit, there is a certain number of members who with their impulsive conduct are causing harm to the VJ as a whole and damage to our unit in particular. "In order to prevent the instances of crime, I hereby order..." and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then follow eight bullet points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were your men familiar with this entire order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, commanding officers had the obligation to familiarise their troops with this order and every other order and information that came down from the superior level, down to the last man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I have already moved to another subject. I request that the documents we have gone through be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have drawn up a report of sorts. It's in tab 481. What is it about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a brief report dated the 4th of April, intended for all members of the unit whereby they are informed that the defence of their homeland, that is Yugoslavia; is being carried out successfully. The NATO expectations to bring Yugoslavia to its knees within two days were not proven right, that the army had suffered minimum losses: In Kursumlija 11, Urosevac 3, Djakovica 1, that they are about to crush Siptar terrorists forces in Jablanica, Istok and Pec, that Siptar terrorist forces are moving with the support of NATO forces from the air, that a court-martial was established in Pristina and it was operational. Several members were already court-martialed in Pristina for offences perpetrated, that it was necessary to prevent looting, that the basic tasks of individuals is to organise defence on assigned routes and directions, to take anti-aircraft protection measures, and to boost combat morale, to prevent defeatism and panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tab 482. You are writing about the data available to the NATO force intended for guiding their airstrikes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information we got from our superior command, namely that within the ranks of the KLA there were members of foreign intelligence and security services, mainly of the US and other NATO member countries, and that according to our information, there had been about 100 SAS members Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. with the task of marking and guiding NATO aviation during their attacks on our forces present on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. In document 483; which deals with military equipment and prisoners, point 4 says, let me not quote everything: "Detention of prisoners, their interrogation by non-specialists or physical threats to them are most strictly prohibited."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This order pertains to both prisoners and to any collection of pieces of aircraft or equipment. It says that pilots who have been shot down or taken prisoner should be handed over to the security organs. And it says also that various objects or intriguing items found in the area may not be collected because they could well be lethal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we move on, a matter of clarification. You'll see at page 52, line 20, the witness gave an answer about a hundred SAS members, whereas if we look at document 482, paragraph 2, the identified 100 people appear to be US special forces. It would obviously help me to know what is being said and of which country's forces at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was saying that they were members of special forces of the United States, in the first paragraph. That's the first paragraph of this report. And in paragraph 2, it says that for a while there have been about 100 members of the SAS force present. SAS, it is well known, belongs to the United Kingdom, not the United States.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clearly written in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I can see it in the original, in which case then there is a clearly an error in the translation of 482A, and we ought to note that there is an error there, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, let us just try to work as expeditiously as possible. What were the tasks related to defence organisation that you yourself set in the form of an order dated the 7th of April in document under 484?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was written again pursuant to an order from the Pristina corps command, and we see from this order that we were to further intensify work on organising the defence of the area in terms of fortification and engineering and the putting up of obstacles in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does the next document pertain to the same thing, 485? It says related to combat documents, the control of various routes and infiltration of Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At all levels of command --" that's the beginning, paragraph 1 -- "draw up the necessary combat documents, conduct a command reconnaissance, and ensure that all officers know their task and that of the neighbouring units." In paragraph 2, it says: "Organise complete control of possible routes by which Siptar terrorist forces may be infiltrated, and ensure effective use of anti-tank devices throughout the defence depth on the routes that are difficult to traverse. "3. Construct two or three positions and installations for the entire combat equipment, relying on populated areas and on dominant features within reach of roads and lateral to the direction of movement of enemy personnel."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In document 486, cluster bombs are mentioned. This is a report dated the 8th of April. Were cluster bombs used in the way that you envisaged?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was massive use of cluster bombs, not only in the border belt but throughout the depth of the territory. It is well known that they were used in attacks against Nis and other cities. As far as my area was concerned, cluster bomb attacks were almost a daily occurrence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 487, it says "Working map of the commander of the 459th Motorised Brigade. "

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my working map. It says "Commencement on the 9th of April."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You also drew up a brief covering the period from the 30th of March to the 7th of April. Is it under tab 488?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is there anything of particular interest here? Does this document reflect current activities?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is sent to units almost on a daily basis. In the introductory part, activities in a broader area are described, that is the general situation in the country, then in our immediate surroundings, and then it goes on to describe activities in the territory of the corps, and finally, towards the end, follows a description of activities of our own unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, each time a map has come out it seemed very neat. Are we seeing the maps that were actually used in the course of the war or are these maps that are copies of what were actually used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a map from the war, and this map here is a copy made in the Military Geographical Institute. This is my working map. It indicates the commencement as the 9th of April, because it was our estimate that at this time a ground offensive of the NATO forces would begin. It shows the deployment of my units. It shows the routes in Albania where Albanian army forces and terrorist forces were concentrated, and this working map of mine was to be marked every day by various symbols depicting activities for that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That particular one that is now on the board is the one that you -- that's the actual copy you used, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a photocopy of my map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So where --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see my signature on it and all the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is the original, the one you actually used? Where is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in Belgrade, in the archive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in document 490, you report something that we could partially see in some of the video footage here, namely a dispatch signed Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. by you on the 14th of April. And you say: "The work of intelligence organs observed in the Ljubizda Has village sector a group of armed men (10-15) was observed in the village holding local people - women, children and the elderly - as hostages." Is that something that we could see in one of those video recordings? Is that the same incident or something similar?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely the event we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this is your dispatch?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's practically a report from my intelligence body that was forwarded to the assistant commander of the Pristina Corps for intelligence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Remind me --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Remind me, General, what did we see on the video relating to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the video we saw the woman and the man talking, that in Prizrenski Has they were staying in a forest and that they held them there for two weeks without giving them water or food.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just go through this information. Is it necessary to dwell on the information of the 15th of April where you inform the command about what happened on the 13th and 14th?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this is information that goes from my command to my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that there are facilities marked by the OSCE where there had been longer stays.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That is on the last page. What does this pertain to, General?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tab 491, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 491. During the night between the 15th and the 14th, the border post of Stojanovic and Liken were attacked by the Apache. Eight persons were killed. And now I say here that these losses could have been prevented had the officers abided by the given instructions, namely that personnel had to be in shelters all the time and that all units should move away from the facilities that had been marked by the OSCE before that. That is to say their standard facilities; border posts, barracks, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. In document 492, support of the Supreme Command to the courage and the morale of the army. Is it necessary to dwell on this in particular?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a letter of support that goes all the way down to the basic units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 494, you give an order that prevents -- that is aimed at preventing surprises in terms of threats to the state border.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order to take immediate measures to completely close axes leading from the territory of Albania into the battalion zones of responsibility and to occupy suitable features and settlements in order to organise defence of the state border and to focus engagement on defence forces in the border area, to fortify defence zones completely in terms of engineering, mass laying of obstacles along the forward defence line, junctures and flanks, make preparations for demolition and third-level fortification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In document 495, you indicate that some omissions were made in the implementation of ordered security measures, and in paragraph 6 you say in particular: "React more quickly and more determinedly against those responsible for looting, crime and indiscipline, and take criminal liability measures against them."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again this order was written on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is your order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Is it necessary to dwell on document 496 where you give an order to leave peacetime location features?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is for the sake of preventing any losses. In part of the barracks there was some quartermaster's -- there was some quartermaster's equipment left, and sometimes personnel would go to get them, and this order is aimed at not doing that any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 497, you provide information about important political landmarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You point out that NATO is trying to prevent the return of Siptar refugees to their homes. Otherwise, the engagement of NATO forces in the heralded, under quotation marks, humanitarian effort would be senseless.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this what your colleagues, what your comrades knew, and those that you were in contact with?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was written right after the last bombing of the column, which took place on the 14th of April, and after various statements, because Jamie Shea, when they admitted that this column of Siptar refugees was bombed by NATO - he was the spokesman of NATO - he said sacrifices had to be made in order to achieve one's ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's time for the break. I'm forming the view that much of this is just general information about the conflict and may not be sufficiently specifically related to the indictment. So when we return from the break, I'd like you to address briefly that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, also one other point related to the last series of documents. In the time I shall take, it obviously won't be possible to explore even a fraction of these documents at all or in detail, and where documents have been skipped over or haven't been referred to, I would ask the Chamber to say they shouldn't be produced. It's not realistic. It may not be realistic to spend any time with the others but it would certainly not be appropriate to produce documents that we haven't looked at at all in the present circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, in the Prosecution case when we had large collections of documents that was a procedure that was often frequently used and Mr. Nice regularly used the phrase that the Court could look at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it in their leisure and refer in a collective term to numbers of documents. When it's clear what the sense of the collective is, that would be, in my submission to the Trial Chamber, a useful and economic way of employing Court time without being too pedantic over the information that's being put before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay. And we have, in fact, sanctioned that approach in relation to Mr. Milosevic. Unless we are persuaded otherwise, I think we'll continue to follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm simply not sure that I ever did this with this type of document. I'm not particularly concerned to thrash the point out now. I am concerned about the fact that there's plainly a quantity of material here that neither I nor probably the Chamber will ever be able to deal with in detail. Had it been served in advance and had it been the subject of some kind of report, things might have been different, but as it is, the Chamber has to decide for itself whether it wants this material in when it will almost certainly not be explored by either side at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm much more concerned about the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, are you referring to the -- those two tabs which were skipped or the other tabs which were briefly touched upon?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think I have to restrict it to those that were skipped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, before the break I was asking you to tell us the relevance of this evidence, which seems to me to be more generally telling the story of the conflict rather than to be specifically relevant to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I am presenting this because I do consider it to be relevant, precisely because it shows a completely different type of behaviour of the army, which fully denies what is contained in Mr. Nice's positions in terms of what the conduct of the army was throughout this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're only interested in conduct of the army insofar as it touches upon a charge in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all of these charges are contained in the indictment, all of it together. I think that's obvious. How else can we establish what it was that the army actually did, why they were at certain locations, how they moved around? You have orders, analyses every time. Their attitude toward the civilian population, also their attitude towards international humanitarian law, the functioning of the army itself, everything else. Now we are to deal with an entire set of criminal reports. Fortunately, there aren't that many of them. The incidents are described in detail, but you can also see exactly how the army acted. Mr. Mice made some assertions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... tabs also deal with that issue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. For example, from tab 500 onwards. I'm going to ask the general to try to go through this as quickly as possible, through these orders of his and the documents that have to do with April and May, to dwell only on some essential elements. Let us move on faster, if you agree, through a certain set of tabs, the one that follows right now, dwelling only on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kay. Perhaps Mr. Kay can refine the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to what we've been looking at, the effect of the NATO bombing on the infrastructure of the country, on the migration of the people, is highly relevant. The Trial Chamber will know that in the indictment there's only, in paragraph 104, one line about the NATO bombing in the indictment. The rest of the indictment concerns the responsibility of Serb forces for the refugees and people crossing the border. In the accused's case, the presentation which shows the effect of NATO bombing, the climate of fear, the concern of the people, its effect upon the movement of peoples, in our submission, is highly relevant to that issue because it was over a sustained period of time. It's not only just the bombing, it's the fact of the overflying aircraft, the number of flights, number of missions leading to that climate of fear that might cause people to leave their homes, which is of course an issue in the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Milosevic. Let us continue as -- proceed as quickly as we can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Robinson. But before I continue, I wanted to ask you what happened to my request to make it possible for me to talk to Mr. Seselj who will be a witness here. For three days in a row now -- I mean, if I'm prevented from seeing him today as well, this is going to be the third day that I will lose in terms of my preparations, without any justification. You know how much you gave me, and now this time that I do have, which is very short, I cannot use very efficiently, and why? Because I simply cannot see the witness for reasons that I'm not going to go into now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, yesterday I instructed the Registrar to present a report on this matter, and I expect that report shortly, perhaps by tomorrow. I will not take any action before I get the report from the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that I'm going to lose three days because of the wait for this report, and maybe a fourth day, too, tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What it means is that the issue that you have raised will not be resolved before the Chamber has the report from the Registrar. That's what it means. Continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in relation to the question pertaining to the authenticity of maps that was put to you by Mr. Bonomy, I wish to say here for the record that I want you to give me a clear answer: Did you personally make these photocopies and did you compare them to your original? Do you claim that these photocopies are fully identical to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. original?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You're quite sure of that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely sure. There are only the additional maps that are called Retimlje that were made in 2002 and that give a more detailed explanation from the 25th until the 28th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All the maps are original?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All are identical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say a photocopy, do you mean that that is a photocopy, at least the two that we can see at the moment, are photocopies, including the writing, of the originals, or are these photocopies onto which the writing has been placed by someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are absolutely copied in their original size and the way they were originally. The Military Institute of Geography has the possibility of making photocopies of this size. So in terms of their size and everything else, they exactly match the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that includes the writing. The writing is a photograph of the original writing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. These four maps were submitted to the Office of the Prosecutor in the beginning of 2003, these four maps here called "Working map of the commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not clear now what you are mean by four now. We've certainly seen more than four.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But just four maps which relate to the working map of the commander, it says, and they begin from March or April 1998, and end - and this is the last map - in April 1999, which shows the incidents on the territory. So there are four such maps. And those maps were sent in at the beginning of 2003 to the Prosecution, and the Prosecution has had them in their possession since that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That also is a photocopy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. But at the time, the investigators of the OTP had the originals in their hands in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And does that apply to the ones on the other side of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is quite a different type of map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed, but the ones on your left-hand side, they also are copies, are they, of what had been used during the conflict, including the writing on the maps? Sorry, I didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything on these maps. This is a photocopy and everything is completely identical. There is absolutely no difference both in terms of format and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is is it a photocopy of everything that was written on the map or is it a map onto which other things have been copied by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It is a copy of everything existing on the original map. Everything that exists on the original map exists on this photocopy map too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there any reason why we can't see at least one of the originals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I am concerned personally, there is no reason, but the maps which are located in the archives are not given out, as far as I know, in the original. That has never been the practice. They are not issued in the original. They are issued either photocopied or photographed and then done to scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We left off discussing document 498, and you talk about cooperation with the court authorities, with the authorities in general, taking care of the population, and so on and so forth. You said that humanitarian conduct should be applied where the civilian population is concerned pursuant to all the provisions of the army of Yugoslavia and international humanitarian law, and you also say that any possible violations will take the most stringent liability measures against anyone in violation of this order. Is that right, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The superior command is requesting that in all units a separate element of combat order should be introduced to take care of the civilian population at the level of the battalions and artillery battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we have here a whole series of documents relating to April, May, and so on, and they are contained in tabs 498 onwards, right up until tab 627, I believe. May we try and go through that material as efficiently and quickly as possible?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I'm concerned, there are no problems there. We can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Then I'm going to ask you to focus on the most important documents and give us your comments, and I'd like to start off with the document contained in tab 500. And we have a criminal report against three individuals, members of your unit from Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that in my area of spot there were two rapes, and this is a criminal report for rape against three soldiers. One was the perpetrator and two assisted the perpetrator, aided and abetted. And these are not men from my unit but from the brigade in Djakovica. And since my military police was territorially responsible, then it compiled the criminal report, and this whole series of documents from the criminal report, the Official Note, the various statements, and later on dating to 2001, we have the military court from Nis which is writing to the district court in Pec with respect to the -- uncovering the perpetrators so they can appear at the military court in Nis. So we had the statements of the women concerned, the injured party.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So we have a rather long set of documents here, including statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we just observe that the date is wrong in the English translation. 17th of April 1999, it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The criminal report is indeed the 17th of April, 1999, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I suggest, Mr. Robinson, that we don't dwell on the individual documents which are attached to this criminal report. I think it's all quite clear, quite clearly set out, so I suggest that we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you move on, Mr. Milosevic, I'd like to find out, what was the outcome of this case, the charges against these three soldiers. Is that revealed --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's ask the General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you can see that. You can see the indictment from the military court dated 1999. And my last piece of information is that the military court, in 2001, in August, appealed to the district court in Pec on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Therefore, they contacted them via the Ministry of Defence, the sector for international military cooperation, in order to, through UNMIK, uncover and find these two women. After that, I don't know what happened, what was done after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't know the result of the trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It was my job to apprehend the perpetrators, to bring them to court and to be handed over to the court with a criminal report. The rest is up to the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, please let's move on now. I have indicated the documents that refer to April and May. Would you please take a look at those documents and draw our attention to what you consider to be important features. For example, in tab 502, there's another criminal report with respect to a theft; and then 503, once again criminal reports relating to theft.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was talking about. It is linked to soldiers who from these columns of refugees took mostly money, and they are criminal reports against them for having perpetrated that act.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. Now, would you be so kind as to go on to the next documents and to do that as efficiently as possible. You have the documents before you, so once again just indicate what you consider to be the most important.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that tab 504 is especially important because it talks about NATO sorties, NATO flights --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, NATO leaflets, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] NATO leaflets that were thrown out in Kosovo and Metohija, and we know that leaflets are classical forms of psychological warfare and propaganda activity. So these leaflets were distributed not in thousands of copies but probably in millions of copies. For each square metre in my area, at least one leaflet was dropped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So there were about 15 different types of leaflets that were dropped. Here we have two types, examples of two types, and I have with me original copies, the original leaflets that were dropped, and if necessary, we can have them placed on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think we need waste time on that. I don't think there is anything contested.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say there was, in my opinion, because these leaflets were dropped on the territory and the population read them. Let me just show you. May I place one leaflet on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is what it says: "A terrible death," is the title. "Projectiles with explosive chambers, such as the Apache rockets known as hell fire and mini bombs of multi-barrel rockets spray the air with metal falling on the population, and usually there is complete combustion that takes place. Return to your families alive. Leave your units and your military equipment. Leave Kosovo and Metohija before it is too late." Another leaflet, for example, or on one of the leaflets you will find my name. There's my name there and the name of the commanders, and on this particular leaflet we have a drawing of the B52 bomber, and it says: "Thousands of bombs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We don't appear to have copies of these.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The heading there is "Thousands of bombs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You say that one had your name on it, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Here it is. That's where my name is. That's the leaflet with my name on it. In all these leaflets, all these leaflets say the same thing: "Leave the territory of Kosovo and Metohija." The leaflets were geared towards soldiers, directed at soldiers, but they had a fantastic effect on the civilian population, a fantastic impact on them because, as I say, they were dropped in such large numbers, enormous numbers, that at least one leaflet dropped on every square metre of territory. And it says: "Don't wait for me. NATO will attack you continuously from all sides."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: However, despite those leaflets, in tab 505 where this piece of information is contained about the situation, on page 2 you say that the combat morale of the forces was very good, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I observe that the leaflets that were just placed on the ELMO are not included in the tab. Or at any rate, one of them is not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have here -- I looked at this a moment ago, is a leaflet which is contained in this tab. Tab 504 contains a leaflet or, rather, there is a piece of information, and attached to it at the end are two or three leaflets. "Don't wait for me," warnings to the forces of the Yugoslav army, NATO, et cetera. All that is contained in tab 504 as an attachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that the one with the general's name?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Tab 622 also has this in B/C/S form. I don't know, of course, whether it's the ones that have been shown, but there is the similar with the photograph of the NATO bomber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think there's a collection of them there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 622, we have several photocopies of the leaflets. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: May we move on, General, please. Shall we try and go through the documents. Would you do your best, please. We left off doing 506 and 505, those were the tabs. But now let's look at the more important ones.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Document 505 is an information, piece of information, a report talking about important political events in the country and in the world and the situation linked to the army and the unit, and it is a report sent out or piece of information that is sent out right down through the battalions, units, and individual companies, down the line to the lowest level. Tab 506 is the next one, and it is procedure for engaging investigative judges on the facilities that were bombed by NATO planes, and recording those, the effects of that operation. 507 is a document for taking additional unit vigilance and combat readiness measures. 508, the next document, is information sent out to the units and linked to the equipment that the NATO pact has in its possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You showed us a leaflet a moment ago with the B52 bomber. According to the combat deployment of your forces, were B52 planes used?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the end of May 1999, 25 times. Those strategic planes bombed 25 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That bombing that you were exposed to by the strategic aviation planes in the border belt, to all intents and purposes, was it in cooperation with any ground attacks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was in cooperation with the aero-ground attack that started at the end of May, and it was direct support and reinforcement to the forces of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many forces, how many men were engaged in that ground attack, that ground operation, when you had these attacks from the strategic air force and planes as well?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, throughout the Pastrik Mountain zone, there were about 4 to 6.000 terrorists, and the strategic planes, after the ground attacks were refuted, the ordinary standard air force would come into play and then the strategic air force would be deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: These were all-out massive ground force attacks, 4 to 6.000 strong, on your positions. Did your units manage successfully to repel all those ground attacks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in one -- on one occasion were they able to break through in depth between 50 -- 500 metres and one kilometre, and we managed to deal with that attack the same day, so those attacks were not successful attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this, General, because it was claimed in certain reports and statements by NATO leaders that there were no ground force attacks across our border, that is to say on our territory.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were ground attacks with the direct participation of the Albanian army. The army of the Republic of Albania took part in them directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the KLA and the army of the Republic of Albania and the strategic planes of the NATO pact; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And all that was in May against our own forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all lasted up until the 7th or 8th of June inclusive, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Could we go on through these other documents. We have finished with 508.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just ask either Mr. Kay or Mr. Nice, are there any charges arising from the attacks in the Pastrik Mountain?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm reluctant to identify an area generally, but I don't think it appears as a name. We'll check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That would be my conclusion too. This was rather like a full-scale battle between two armed forces. Yes, proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we left off on tab 510. Should we deal with it in detail? It is a warning.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there's any need to do that. This is a warning related to general conduct and prevention of unlawful conduct. The same as tab 511. It speaks of incidents involving loss of life in ambushes and attacks, and members of the units are instructed to be more careful to prevent that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Follows a document concerning measures for boosting morale and psychological preparation and improving combat readiness. Tab 513, taking measures to protect units and prevent penetration by enemy forces. Tab 14, description of the general political situation.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the sort of daily brief that was sent to all units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then another warning to raise the level of security, 515. And in 516, the Chief of Staff Colonel Vladimir Stojiljkovic sent this intelligence report to the command of the 549th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is about information collected by intelligence organs primarily about events in the territory of the Republic of Albania, information that was collected by observation from our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about 517? What does this report contain?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report that was made available to all members of the unit. In the introduction, as usual -- the focus is actually on the fact that a large number of volunteers signed up in various towns of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that among the volunteers there were people who had come from abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, what's in these criminal reports in 518, 519? These are criminal reports against conscripts who had perpetrated certain criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case with 518. 519 is a criminal report against an unidentified perpetrator, and it concerns the kidnapping of five of my soldiers on the 11th of April on the road between Prizren and Suva Reka. That is why this is against an unidentified perpetrator. These soldiers were kidnapped by Siptar terrorists. It was a group of five, and two of them were escorting the kidnapped men to a court-martial. Their fate -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. they have never been heard from again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this procedure -- these measures were taken in the course of abiding by the law.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We know that they were kidnapped somewhere on the road. We know it was done by a group of terrorists based in the area of Budakovo, but as for what happened to these people, we don't know anything yet, although new and new graves are being found in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This next document under 520 is your order, which, as a follow-up to this incident, instructs which measures should be taken to prevent such incidents.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It instructs people never to leave their area of deployment unauthorised and to take all measures of security required to avoid such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to go through the most important documents.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 521 is my report to the command of the Pristina Corps to the effect that the territorial military organs, military sections, in other words, relocated from population centres. 522 says that all the materiel collected, such as food, fuel, and other materiel collected from private persons should be properly recorded and stored.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, tell me, what does this order refer to? It was taken pursuant to an order from the Pristina Corps command. In 525 it mentioned defence stabilisation measures in the zone of your command, control over the territory. In paragraph 2 it says: "In receiving, dispersing and providing security for the civilian population act in line with the previously issued orders of the brigade command. Prevent any undisciplined behaviour on the part of commanding officers in relation to the civilian population."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in line with the previous order concerning civilians where paragraph 1 deals with control over the territory, paragraph 2 treatment of civilian population and their accommodation, paragraph 3 clearing of the territory, paragraph 4 organisation of administration and self-government and organisation of some sort of Crisis Staffs. It says that units of labour obligation should be set up to clear the territory, sanitise the territory, clear the rubble left by airstrikes by NATO, measures to combat crime and maximise the lawfulness of conduct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Measures of logistical support. It says that this is a standing order and that commanders of immediately subordinate units are directly responsible for its implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please go on.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 526 also describes the situation generally in the world and in our country and our specific situation within the unit. 527 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Some of these are not translated. I gather they're going a bit fast for the interpreters. Frankly, it's fairly fast for somebody who hasn't got a text to read. It's quite fast even when you have got a text to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic and the witness, please bear that in mind. Some of the documents are not translated, and you must observe a pause between the question and answer for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us go through the most important of these documents, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So 527 is an intelligence report from my intelligence body to the intelligence body of the corps. It says that still on the border crossing of Vrbnica large groups of journalists with cameras are still present, and that there are also vehicles with satellite aerials which beam their reports from the border crossing immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the relevance of this, Mr. Milosevic, this intelligence report, to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is indirectly linked to the departure of refugees from our territory. You can see that the various bodies in our army were fully conscious that everything was being done within the system of propaganda to create a humanitarian catastrophe, and we know what kind of reports were sent and why allegedly Albanians left Kosovo and Metohija. You can see the organisation and the linkage of the war machine with the media machinery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 528.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second. We will consult on the relevance of this particular item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the basis that it relates to the question of refugees, we will allow it, but I must say that a lot of this is only marginally useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are there likely to be Albanian witnesses coming here to tell us that they left because of NATO bombing?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they said so many times, but there will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, the answer's incomplete on the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked whether I will call them. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're nearing the end of your Kosovo case. Please bear in mind what I said yesterday, that you have now used up about half of the time allocated to you, and you're still dealing with first of three parts of the case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, as you know, you are in control of the time. I told you that my time is insufficient, and I do not have the impression that I am disposing of it irrationally. I didn't call God knows how many witnesses testifying, as this witness is, about the totality of the operation of the army with these documents which account for only 6 per cent of all the documents that General Delic could bring, that is over 10.000 documents. We have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let us proceed. You are in charge of the use of your time. You must manage your time as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the extremely difficult and totally groundless allegations that we heard here about the conduct of the army -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I do not want a speech. I do not want a speech. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, beginning with the tab 530 onwards, we have a series of documents covering the month of May. Could you please give us only the most pertinent highlights. Just the most important things that you can --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 532 is another report not unlike the previous ones sent to my units. 533 is an order, an order to improve the system of command in order to ensure complete control over personnel, and an uncompromisingly proper appearance of all members of the brigade. 534 is another intelligence report which says: "During the day on many occasions groups of refugees crossed the border. Once they crossed the border, foreign journalists gather them immediately, interview them, and then bus them or transport them in trucks further on. It has been observed that better quality cars were taken to the side by men dressed in black suits."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: These were your observations of what was going on on the other side of the border?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: 535 is another intelligence report, where it says in paragraph 2: "The armed forces of Albania in the areas of their bunkers continue to clear them and to build shelters for their personnel. After airstrikes by NATO against the town of Prizren, large migration of the population has been observed." Tab 536. On the 29th of April, 1999, two cluster projectiles were aimed at personnel from the block house of Krstac, hurting one commanding officer and three soldiers. 537, again an intelligence report that was sent to the Pristina Corps, and it records what was observed on the Albanian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. Will it hurt a lot if we just skip the next few tabs which deal with those daily incidents and your daily activities in order to dwell a little on 552, which mentions cluster bombs and various types of charges and the use of prohibited weapons?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be all right. Perhaps would I like at another one before that. You said 552?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 552 it says that: "So far NATO Air Force has been using different projectiles, cluster bombs with different charges as of late, and charges that are vibration activated," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information to all members of the unit. Since as the end of April was nearing, as well as the month of May, every day many cluster projectiles were used. Even some new bombs were used. That is not stated in this document, but it is in others. CBU-99, and we did not have any information about that. So we would therefore -- or, rather, we did therefore caution that these objects should not be touched. 15 to 20 per cent of all cluster bombs were not activated. They remained there, and later on they could be activated if somebody walked up to them or touched them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in document 555, you have documentation about crimes, criminal offences, signed by your assistant commander, Lieutenant Colonel Vlada Milankovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is my assistant commander for information and moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you say: "At the very outset, and particularly as the war operations in Kosovo and Metohija gain momentum, the number and type of criminal offences subject to more severe sanctions in wartime has seen a sharp rise; some of them were qualified as war crimes and treated in the most stringent way, especially since there is no statute of limitation for this type of crime. "Then the activation of judicial organs is concerned and the work of investigation and security organs in the units, the perpetrators have been investigated, prosecuted and convicted more promptly and efficiently for crimes relating to military service..." Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then there is further mention of the percentages. "By far the highest percentage in the report of criminal offences involve the following..." It says murder, and then aggravated theft, stressing the sentence that is envisaged, then taking a vehicle, and wilful abandonment and desertion of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then two paragraphs down, it says: "Criminal reports against 297 individuals were filed with the military prosecutor attached to the PRK command; the military court received 95 indictments; and requests for investigation of 109 individuals were submitted. Of the total number of criminal reports filed, 22 involved officers, 30 non-commissioned officers, 227 privates, 15 civilians, and 3 unidentified persons."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this is the 12th of May. Is this the time when the operations against our forces were the fiercest?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fiercest fighting was in the area of Kosare, between Djakovica and Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the time when the fiercest fighting was going on involving several thousands of persons attacking your units, you are acting lawfully and prosecuting criminal offences. This is the 12th of May when this information is being provided.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On page 2 of this information there is reference to the corps and also to my own unit, the criminal reports that were filed up to then from the 24th of May until the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is very relevant. Do we know the kind of offences for which the soldiers were charged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a survey. On page 2, if you look at page 2, these are my soldiers. There is an exact reference here as to why, what the type of criminal offence charged was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. That's theft, wounding, rape, negligent performance, illegal crossing of the state border, wilful abandonment of duty during combat, desertion, terrorism, infliction of bodily injury, and failure to discharge one's duty during combat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in your area of responsibility, was there a single criminal offence that your organs had learned about and that legal action was not taken about? Rather, had the perpetrator not been arrested in any case if committing an offence for which arrests are envisaged? Is there a single case?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a single case that we did not act in accordance with the law if we knew of any particular case. Even after the war, on the basis of subsequent knowledge, certain criminal reports were filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In tab 562 -- I'm trying to deal with this as quickly as possible, but you draw my attention to anything that I may have omitted that is of capital importance. In 562, you talk about Tusus, the KLA headquarters there.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 559. Tab 559 is something I would deal with. It speaks of a visit by foreign journalists during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They visited Prizren?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that from this paper which is sent to the command of the Pristina Corps, the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They recorded NATO airstrikes at certain locations; the village of Jablanica, then two residential areas in town. It says here that they talked to random passersby because they were interested in statements primarily of ethnic Albanians. Foreign journalists were surprised by how lively the town was, as opposed to Pristina. They emphasised that Pristina was a dead city, and they also commented on the ethnic diversity of the town, the population of the town, in spite of all the troubles. The Italians visited the monastery and spent some time there recording and taking pictures. Other foreigners recorded mosques, and yet others interviewed two politicians who lived here; the president of the Democratic Reform Party of Albania, Sokol Qusha, and the president of the Roma Democratic Party, Ljuan Koka, who were also members of the state delegation of Serbia during the political talks in Rambouillet. The essence of the statement has to do with a halt to the NATO bombing, resolution of the problem by peaceful and political means, and equal respect for the interests of all the ethnic communities. When touring the border, as they moved towards the border, they saw 80 to 100 people moving in a refugee column. Then NATO aircraft bombed right next to this column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just go on here. The refugees stated that nobody had beat them, that they were afraid of bombs. If they could, they would return to their homes straight away, that some Albanians went from one of their houses to the other, ordering them to go to Albania. The Rai Uno journalist asked the man who was leading the whole group whether he stood by these statements and whether he would give his name, at which the mentioned person took out his ID card without a word and gave it to the journalist so he could take down the necessary details, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a reference, General, to heaps of registration plates removed from vehicles and to a heap of personal documents. Can you tell me what that's about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was with this group and I was at the border myself at the time. I noticed that at the border there were quite a few registration plates that were taken off. That is what I noticed primarily. I didn't see the documents. After returning, I went back to the head of the Secretariat of the Ministry of the Interior, and I asked him whether he knew about this and why this was being done. He said that he had no knowledge about this, that it came as news to him, and that he would take measures immediately. After this, it did not happen again. I think that this was simply arbitrary behaviour on the part of the persons working at the border crossing. The border post continued to function, and the border policemen and customs officials were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's also reference to film of the events being broadcast on foreign television stations. That's at the end of the -- very end of the document. Can I take it that that's a reference to genuine --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- objective reports of these events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, these were journalists who came to the zone and who filmed what they wanted to. These were journalists from -- from Brussels. There was a Belgian TV crew, and Rai from Italy. And then Frans De Smit (de Standaard), probably journalists in the evening. "At 10.00 p.m.," it says, "on foreign news broadcasts (especially the BBC, Sky, and others) there were reports filmed by these journalists at the border crossing." It's interesting that these journalists who were on our side of the border met the journalists who were on the Albanian side of the border at the border itself and that they spent a short period of time talking to each other because they came from the same media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Milosevic, we are going to adjourn now. We will adjourn and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 7th day of July, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
